subject: PO metadata, invoice format and net terms for Parkview pilot
messages:
From: Elena Park <epark@parkviewhealth.com>
To: jonas.weber@redwood.com
Date: Tue, Feb 9, 2027 at 10:12 AM -0800
Subject: PO fields + monthly billing cadence for Parkview pilot

Jonas,

Thanks for the demo last week — team is excited to get the pilot going. Procurement asked me to confirm a few things before they issue the PO. Please see the checklist below and let me know what you can accept on the PO and in the invoice PDF we send to AP: 

- Required PO header fields: PO Number, Bill-to legal entity name, Parkview GL code (we'll supply), Cost Center, Project Code (if applicable)
- Invoicing cadence: monthly invoices by the 1st of the month for the prior month
- Invoice format: PDF with the PO number on the first page and line-item mapping to SKU/usage; include Redwood Tax ID and remit-to address
- Net terms: Parkview default is Net60 for new vendors; would Redwood accept Net60 for the pilot?
- Vendor setup: please complete Parkview vendor onboarding form (attached) and return with vendor tax info

Attaching Parkview_PO_Template.xlsx to make sure fields match.

If Net60 is a hard blocker, we can escalate — but ideally we want the pilot on standard Parkview terms.

Thanks,
Elena Park
Senior Procurement Analyst
Parkview Health

Attachment: Parkview_PO_Template.xlsx (Excel, 34KB)

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Elena Park <epark@parkviewhealth.com>
Cc: kimberly.park@redwood.com
Date: Tue, Feb 9, 2027 at 11:08 AM -08:00
Subject: Re: PO fields + monthly billing cadence for Parkview pilot

Elena —

Appreciate the clear checklist and the template. We can meet most of those requirements. Quick summary and a couple of follow-ups: 

- PO header fields: we can include PO number, bill-to legal entity, remit-to address, Redwood Tax ID and a custom field for Project Code. Confirm the exact GL code mapping when you have it.
- Invoice PDF: we will include the PO number on page 1 and line-item SKUs mapped to usage buckets (pilot SKU vs overage).
- Invoicing cadence: monthly invoices delivered by the 1st for prior month is fine.
- Net terms: our standard is Net30. For pilots we can accept Net45 as a concession, or Net60 with a one-time prepay holdback of 10% until the first invoice clears. Would you be open to Net45 for 90 days, then revisit on expansion?

I'll loop in Kim from Finance to confirm the remittance details and any vendor setup forms we need to fill on our side. Also happy to sign the DocuSign order form if you send it.

Next steps:
1) Can you confirm whether Parkview can accept Net45 for the pilot?
2) Share final GL and cost-center mapping for invoice line allocation.
3) If Parkview needs Net60, we can propose the 10% holdback approach or an advance partial payment.

Best,
Jonas Weber
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

--

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Elena Park <epark@parkviewhealth.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, Feb 10, 2027 at 08:56 AM -08:00
Subject: RE: PO fields + monthly billing cadence for Parkview pilot

Elena —

Thanks for the details; Kim from Finance here. We reviewed internally and can offer the following for the pilot (to keep things moving):

- Net terms: We can accept Net45 for the pilot period (90 days), provided the PO includes the Parkview PO Number and the following vendor fields: Redwood legal name, Redwood Tax ID (EIN 12-3456789), remit-to address (see vendor profile).
- Holdback: If Parkview must have Net60 as a policy, we can accept Net60 with a 10% holdback on the first invoice only (released after payment clears) or an advance of 25% of the first month as an alternative.
- Invoice layout: Please ensure each invoice PDF includes the PO number as "PO:" in the top-right header and a single-line summary per SKU/category matching the Parkview template. Supporting CSV can be attached for AP system ingestion.
- Remit/ERP mapping: We require the PO to include the Parkview AP account code and cost center to avoid rejections.

I've attached a filled vendor setup PDF with remit-to details (Redwood_Vendor_Profile.pdf). Can you confirm which option you prefer (Net45 vs Net60+holdback vs prepay)? Also, do you have a DocuSign order form link so we can review the commercial terms and attach the PO as an exhibit?

Regards,
Kimberly Park
Director, Finance Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachment: Redwood_Vendor_Profile.pdf (PDF, 28KB)

--

Date: Thu, Feb 11, 2027 at 09:04 AM -08:00
Subject: Re: PO metadata, invoice format and net terms for Parkview pilot

Kim, Jonas —

Thanks for the fast turnaround. Procurement talked to AP and we can do Net45 for the pilot if Redwood signs the DocuSign order and includes the required PO header fields. Parkview will issue a single monthly invoice on the 1st; AP needs the invoice PDF plus an attached CSV for ingestion.

We are attaching a signed PO stub to confirm the start date and the PO number will be generated by next Tuesday. For future expansion, I noted your ask about Net30 for annual deals — that's something we can discuss with Procurement leadership during renewal/expansion. For now, Net45 works.

Action items I have for Redwood: 
- Upload the vendor profile and respond with the DocuSign order link or a draft order form we can sign
- Confirm remit-to address and Redwood Tax ID in the vendor profile we received (Kim attached)
- Confirm you will include CSV support for AP ingestion on each invoice PDF

I'll attach Parkview_PO_Signed_Stub.pdf for reference.

Best,
Elena Park
Senior Procurement Analyst
Parkview Health
